profile.themes: Festive + wedding seasonality (Q3 = festive; Q4 = best quarter / wedding season). Demand "occasion-driven", spikes limited to key events

bull_bear.body:
- **Second interim dividend of ₹3/share** (face value ₹2) declared.
- Disciplined/"prudent" capital allocation; legacy cash funds retail rollout; "well within comfort limit" on debt.
- Finance cost up YoY due to extra working capital for inventory build; expected to improve by Q4 end.
- Open to partnerships/acquisitions but nothing currently planned; focus on existing retail brands.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Demand:** weak/occasion-driven discretionary spend; cautious consumer, moderate footfall.
- **Seasonality / timing:** Diwali timing skew distorts quarterly reads; heavy Q4 dependence.
- **Retail execution:** nascent ZECODE/DEVO, sourcing & gross-margin challenges, lean team, near-term EBITDA drag (100–150 bps).
- **Cost:** new labour-code one-off; elevated ad spend; higher working capital → finance cost.
- **Competition:** large unorganized apparel market (sees as headroom, not direct threat); fabric segment has few branded peers / no pricing pressure cited.
- Note: textile growth (~3% Q3) lagged peer Raymond (~11%) — attributed to Diwali timing.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Measured, disciplined, defensive on QoQ ("not advisable to look quarterly — seasonal business"), confident on raised FY26 guidance. Cautious/transparent on retail being early-stage; declines to give store-level economics or FY27 numbers yet. Emphasis on calibrated, efficiency-first retail expansion ("not chasing numbers").
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- FY26 revenue guidance UPGRADE (10–12% → 12–15%) called "an exception" given their usual annual-only stance — notable positive signal.
- Exports are **indirect** (fabric → converters → brands); FTA benefit is second-order, not direct shipment to EU brands.
- Larger-format stores (6,000–8,000 sq ft) chosen after explicit A/B experiment vs small format.
- Indigo yarn business quietly grown to ~5–6% within Yarn & Others.
- Q3 store openings deliberately throttled to protect festive operations (lean team) — Q2 front-loaded the openings.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- 48-year heritage (founded 1978) with strong brand recall and consumer trust across price tiers
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning fabrics and apparel — Siyaram's, J. Hampstead, Cadini, Oxemberg and Mistair — plus newer retail brands ZECODE and DEVO
- Integrated manufacturing footprint across Tarapur, Daman, Amravati and Silvassa enabling quality control, scale and speed
- Wide distribution reach — distributors, franchises, multi-brand outlets, exclusive stores, online marketplaces and institutional engagements across 36 states/UTs and 21 export countries
- In-house design studio and R&D team converting consumer/trend insight into commercially successful ranges
- Asset-light production model combining in-house capacity with outsourcing, allowing flexible volumes at lower capital intensity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Microeconomic / domestic-demand concentration risk — The Company derives the majority of its revenue from the domestic market, with exports a relatively small share of total sales, making it more exposed to domestic economic conditions — consumer demand shifts, inflation, interest rates, input-cost fluctuations, competitive intensity and government policy changes.
- Market demand uncertainty — Persistently elevated inflation may soften demand in both domestic and international markets, reducing sales and profitability; performing across multiple segments adds complexity as the Company must meet evolving customer requirements amid intense pricing pressure.
- Raw material price risk — Fluctuating raw material prices directly affect the Company's input-cost structure, and stiff competitive intensity can limit its ability to pass on higher prices, which can significantly impact profitability.
- Shifting consumer/fashion trends risk — The textile and apparel sector continuously evolves with rapidly changing consumer preferences (including sustainability trends); an inability to integrate quickly poses a competitiveness risk.
- Reputational risk from counterfeiting — The textile industry faces significant challenges from proliferating counterfeit products, causing losses to both purchasers and legitimate sellers, undermining brand value and affecting the sentiment of customers who pay a premium for genuine products.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Festive demand picked up at start of quarter, then customers turned cautious, footfall moderate; demand **occasion/festive-driven**, spikes at key events, not a sustained trend.
- Discretionary spend high in festive season across BOTH premium and mass/value fabrics — "more festive driven than price-point driven"; value audience much larger → larger numbers.
- New retail growing faster than traditional business; "very encouraging" wedding-season traction for ZECODE/DEVO, better footfall and repeat customers.
business.title: Demand

business.body:
- **Fabric (78%):** Suiting (poly-viscose to woollen blends) + shirting (polycotton, cotton, linen blends); few branded players, **no meaningful pricing pressure**; gross-margin moves driven by product mix. ~9% 9M volume growth. Has been declining as % (from >80% historically) as other segments scale.
- **Garment / branded apparel (15%):** Siyaram's, J.Hampstead, Oxemberg branded business.
- **Yarn & Others (7%):** Includes an **Indigo business growing to ~5–6%**.
- **New retail — ZECODE & DEVO:** First full year of operation; nascent, more stores opening than running; ₹55 cr in 9M; offline-only for now (no e-commerce yet); large-format (6,000–8,000 sq ft) preferred over small (4,000–6,000) after experimentation; regional clusters (ZECODE in one region, DEVO in another); sourcing/gross-margin still a start-up challenge.

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA margin 13.2% (−90 bps YoY) on: new labour-code employee one-off, higher ad/sales promotion, retail start-up losses (~₹10–12 cr combined ex-retail-loss items).
- **Marketing/ad spend guided at 4–5% of revenue** (includes both legacy and new brands; new brands more regional/digital) — treated as brand-building investment.
- Gross margin up ~3% YoY on product mix (mgmt expects balanced/stable full-year).
- Processing & labour charges rose ~14%→15% of net sales due to inventory build for Q4.
- Steady-state retail margin not yet disclosed (sourcing/gross-margin challenges; will share "in a few quarters").
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q3 FY26 (this call):** Total income ₹639 cr (+8.9% YoY); EBITDA ₹84 cr (+1.5%), margin 13.2% (−90 bps); PAT ₹42 cr (−8.7%), margin 6.6%. Mix Fabric 78% / Garment 15% / Yarn&Others 7%. FY26 rev guidance RAISED 10–12% → 12–15%; EBITDA ~14% ex-retail, −100/150 bps retail drag. Retail ₹55 cr/9M vs ₹70–80 cr FY26 target; stores ZECODE 25 / DEVO 17 (added 2+5 in Q3); ~35-store FY26 plan. 2nd interim dividend ₹3/sh. One-offs: new labour-code employee cost + higher ad spend (~₹10–12 cr) + retail start-up losses. FY27 guidance deferred to next quarter.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **FY26 revenue growth RAISED to 12–15%** (from prior 10–12%) — overall company. Described as "an exception" to their usual annual-only guidance.
- **FY26 EBITDA margin ~14%** (approx, ex-retail), to be reduced by **100–150 bps** from retail (ZECODE/DEVO) losses.
- **Retail (ZECODE+DEVO) revenue ₹70–80 cr for FY26** — ₹55 cr done in 9M; on track / in line.
- **Store rollout: ~35 ZECODE+DEVO stores in FY26.** ~22 opened YTD; Q3 added only 2 ZECODE + 5 DEVO (intentionally slow to focus ops on festive). Cumulative: ZECODE 25, DEVO 17. Balance to be opened by March (possible spillover).
- Fabric volume growth **~9% (9M FY26)**; suiting vs shirting differ — mgmt prefers value over volume reads.
- **FY27 guidance (revenue, margin, store plans, new geographies) deferred to next quarter.**
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **Branded value-retail scale-up (ZECODE/DEVO)** — calibrated, self-owned model; expects to become a "meaningful part" of turnover over years; e-commerce/omnichannel "at the back of our minds" for later.
- **Exports (~9–10%, largely fabric to converters):** Beneficiary of India-as-manufacturing-hub narrative, govt manufacturing push, and **new FTAs (incl. European FTA)** — indirect benefit (fabric supplied to garment converters who serve brands).
- **Forward integration:** Exploring expansion of **garment infrastructure to supply formal trousers** (not just suiting fabric) → could become a direct supplier; "some time away".
- **CADINI (Italian brand/subsidiary):** exposes company to European fashion/trends, feeds design USP.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale ZECODE (fast fashion) and DEVO (ethnic wear) through a company-owned, company-operated, cluster-based store rollout — prioritising store density, operating-model maturity and store-level productivity over rapid national expansion
- Strengthen the core fabric and apparel (legacy) business while expanding the retail footprint with discipline
- Combine national-scale media for established brands with sharper, localised digital, influencer and in-store marketing for the newer retail brands to deepen consumer connect
- Maintain an asset-light manufacturing model — an optimum mix of in-house capacity and outsourcing — to flex volumes with demand at lower capital intensity
- Deploy capital prudently, balancing growth investment with healthy margins, efficient operations and shareholder returns
- Grow exports in absolute terms from the current base over the medium to long term as global trade conditions and trade-agreement access improve
- Orient the ZECODE format increasingly toward larger stores (6,000-10,000 sq ft) based on stronger early performance of bigger formats, subject to location availability
- Extend DEVO's North India cluster beyond Delhi and Uttar Pradesh into Punjab, deepening density before entering new catchments
- Value creation is viewed with a long-term lens: the Company pays out dividends regularly (three interim dividends plus a Board-recommended final dividend for FY26) while retaining flexibility to reinvest in future growth; financial discipline centres on balancing growth investment with healthy margins, efficient operations and sustainable returns. For FY26 the Board did not recommend any transfer of profit to reserves, carrying the full year's profit forward to the Statement of Profit and Loss. Retail expansion (ZECODE/DEVO stores) is being funded through the Company's internal accruals/strength rather than external capital.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Retail expansion: the company added 25 new stores across its ZECODE (fast fashion) and DEVO (ethnic wear) formats during FY26, taking the year-end network to 44 company-owned stores (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO) with a combined retail footprint of over 2.50 lakh sq ft; ZECODE is clustered around Bengaluru/Karnataka and DEVO around Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and now Punjab, and management intends to take the combined store count to approximately 70 in FY27, funded through internal accruals. Real-estate diversification: the company has launched a one-off residential development on its idle MIDC leasehold residential plot at Dombivali, with a total constructed area of approximately 77,000 sq ft. Sustainability capex: the company has commissioned captive rooftop solar power plants across its manufacturing units (total installed solar capacity of 6,792 kWp across all plants) and is upgrading outdated machinery to modern, energy-efficient equipment and transitioning its vehicle fleet from petrol/diesel to electric vehicles.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Consumer demand was uneven through FY26 — early-year softness from seasonal disruption and cautious discretionary spending, restored momentum in festive/wedding periods, and gradual improvement toward year-end supported by tax reform measures and higher spending around key consumption periods
- India's consumption story is seen as a meaningful long-term opportunity, supported by rising aspirations, improving incomes, a growing preference for branded products and expanding retail infrastructure
- Industry continues to navigate elevated input and logistics costs, inflationary pressures and an evolving geopolitical environment as cost/margin headwinds
- Domestic demand remains sensitive to discretionary spending patterns and inflation, with a shift toward value pricing pressuring margins in mass-market apparel
- Man-made fibre (MMF) segment is a structural growth driver for the textile industry, supported by the PLI Scheme for Textiles and GST rationalisation that reduced GST on MMF fibres/yarns to 5%, improving working capital efficiency
- India-EU and India-UK Free Trade Agreements are expected to significantly benefit the sector via zero/reduced import duties, with Indian apparel exports to the EU projected to grow 20-25% YoY after FTA operationalisation (versus a current ~3.01% growth rate), placing Indian exporters on par with Bangladesh and Vietnam
- Global brands' 'China+1' sourcing shift is strengthening India's position as a reliable manufacturing hub, supporting export opportunity
- Exports have remained stable at around 10% of company revenue and are viewed as a medium-to-long-term growth opportunity as trade conditions stabilise
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Integrated blended-fabric + branded-apparel player using cash-generative legacy fabric business to fund a calibrated, self-owned value fast-fashion retail rollout (ZECODE/DEVO); Q3 was a soft, occasion-driven festive quarter with margin pressure from one-offs and early-stage retail losses, but FY26 revenue guidance was RAISED to 12–15%.

risks.note: The Company derives the majority of its revenue from the domestic market, with exports a relatively small share of total sales, making it more exposed to domestic economic conditions — consumer demand shifts, inflation, interest rates, input-cost fluctuations, competitive intensity and government policy changes.

Persistently elevated inflation may soften demand in both domestic and international markets, reducing sales and profitability; performing across multiple segments adds complexity as the Company must meet evolving customer requirements amid intense pricing pressure.

Fluctuating raw material prices directly affect the Company's input-cost structure, and stiff competitive intensity can limit its ability to pass on higher prices, which can significantly impact profitability.
The textile and apparel sector continuously evolves with rapidly changing consumer preferences (including sustainability trends); an inability to integrate quickly poses a competitiveness risk.

The textile industry faces significant challenges from proliferating counterfeit products, causing losses to both purchasers and legitimate sellers, undermining brand value and affecting the sentiment of customers who pay a premium for genuine products.

thesis (one-liner): Integrated blended-fabric + branded-apparel player using cash-generative legacy fabric business to fund a calibrated, self-owned value fast-fashion retail rollout (ZECODE/DEVO); Q3 was a soft, occasion-driven festive quarter with margin pressure from one-offs and early-stage retail losses, but FY26 revenue guidance was RAISED to 12–15%.
scorecard (q3 fy26):

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | ₹639 cr | ₹586 cr | +8.9% | Festive demand picked up early then footfall moderated; "occasion-driven" |

**Revenue by segment (Q3 mix):** Fabric 78%, Garment 15%, Yarn & Others 7% (Indigo ~5–6% within Yarn & Others). Exports ~9–10% of revenue, largely fabric.

**Seasonality CALL-OUT:** Highly seasonal — mgmt repeatedly discouraged QoQ reads. Diwali timing (early in Q3) shifted festive sales into Q2, depressing Q3 textile growth (~3% YoY) vs strong 9M. **Q4 is "the best quarter of the year"** (wedding season); inventory being built up for it (drove higher working capital & processing/labour charges).

**One-offs (explicit, ~₹10–12 cr combined drag):** (1) onetime employee expense from the **new labour code**; (2) higher **advertising & sales promotion**; (3) **new-retail (ZECODE/DEVO) start-up losses** (in line with guided 100–150 bps EBITDA drag).
guidance (critical):
- **FY26 revenue growth RAISED to 12–15%** (from prior 10–12%) — overall company. Described as "an exception" to their usual annual-only guidance.
- **FY26 EBITDA margin ~14%** (approx, ex-retail), to be reduced by **100–150 bps** from retail (ZECODE/DEVO) losses.
- **Retail (ZECODE+DEVO) revenue ₹70–80 cr for FY26** — ₹55 cr done in 9M; on track / in line.
- **Store rollout: ~35 ZECODE+DEVO stores in FY26.** ~22 opened YTD; Q3 added only 2 ZECODE + 5 DEVO (intentionally slow to focus ops on festive). Cumulative: ZECODE 25, DEVO 17. Balance to be opened by March (possible spillover).
- Fabric volume growth **~9% (9M FY26)**; suiting vs shirting differ — mgmt prefers value over volume reads.
- **FY27 guidance (revenue, margin, store plans, new geographies) deferred to next quarter.**
demand:
- Festive demand picked up at start of quarter, then customers turned cautious, footfall moderate; demand **occasion/festive-driven**, spikes at key events, not a sustained trend.
- Discretionary spend high in festive season across BOTH premium and mass/value fabrics — "more festive driven than price-point driven"; value audience much larger → larger numbers.
- New retail growing faster than traditional business; "very encouraging" wedding-season traction for ZECODE/DEVO, better footfall and repeat customers.
segment detail:
- **Fabric (78%):** Suiting (poly-viscose to woollen blends) + shirting (polycotton, cotton, linen blends); few branded players, **no meaningful pricing pressure**; gross-margin moves driven by product mix. ~9% 9M volume growth. Has been declining as % (from >80% historically) as other segments scale.
- **Garment / branded apparel (15%):** Siyaram's, J.Hampstead, Oxemberg branded business.
- **Yarn & Others (7%):** Includes an **Indigo business growing to ~5–6%**.
- **New retail — ZECODE & DEVO:** First full year of operation; nascent, more stores opening than running; ₹55 cr in 9M; offline-only for now (no e-commerce yet); large-format (6,000–8,000 sq ft) preferred over small (4,000–6,000) after experimentation; regional clusters (ZECODE in one region, DEVO in another); sourcing/gross-margin still a start-up challenge.
growth / optionality:
- **Branded value-retail scale-up (ZECODE/DEVO)** — calibrated, self-owned model; expects to become a "meaningful part" of turnover over years; e-commerce/omnichannel "at the back of our minds" for later.
- **Exports (~9–10%, largely fabric to converters):** Beneficiary of India-as-manufacturing-hub narrative, govt manufacturing push, and **new FTAs (incl. European FTA)** — indirect benefit (fabric supplied to garment converters who serve brands).
- **Forward integration:** Exploring expansion of **garment infrastructure to supply formal trousers** (not just suiting fabric) → could become a direct supplier; "some time away".
- **CADINI (Italian brand/subsidiary):** exposes company to European fashion/trends, feeds design USP.
margins & cost:
- EBITDA margin 13.2% (−90 bps YoY) on: new labour-code employee one-off, higher ad/sales promotion, retail start-up losses (~₹10–12 cr combined ex-retail-loss items).
- **Marketing/ad spend guided at 4–5% of revenue** (includes both legacy and new brands; new brands more regional/digital) — treated as brand-building investment.
- Gross margin up ~3% YoY on product mix (mgmt expects balanced/stable full-year).
- Processing & labour charges rose ~14%→15% of net sales due to inventory build for Q4.
- Steady-state retail margin not yet disclosed (sourcing/gross-margin challenges; will share "in a few quarters").
capex:
- **Legacy: asset-light, maintenance capex ~₹50–70 cr/year** (sufficient internal cash flow).
- **Retail: ~₹35–40 cr for FY26** (calibrated).
capital allocation:
- **Second interim dividend of ₹3/share** (face value ₹2) declared.
- Disciplined/"prudent" capital allocation; legacy cash funds retail rollout; "well within comfort limit" on debt.
- Finance cost up YoY due to extra working capital for inventory build; expected to improve by Q4 end.
- Open to partnerships/acquisitions but nothing currently planned; focus on existing retail brands.
risks:
- **Demand:** weak/occasion-driven discretionary spend; cautious consumer, moderate footfall.
- **Seasonality / timing:** Diwali timing skew distorts quarterly reads; heavy Q4 dependence.
- **Retail execution:** nascent ZECODE/DEVO, sourcing & gross-margin challenges, lean team, near-term EBITDA drag (100–150 bps).
- **Cost:** new labour-code one-off; elevated ad spend; higher working capital → finance cost.
- **Competition:** large unorganized apparel market (sees as headroom, not direct threat); fabric segment has few branded peers / no pricing pressure cited.
- Note: textile growth (~3% Q3) lagged peer Raymond (~11%) — attributed to Diwali timing.
management tone: Measured, disciplined, defensive on QoQ ("not advisable to look quarterly — seasonal business"), confident on raised FY26 guidance. Cautious/transparent on retail being early-stage; declines to give store-level economics or FY27 numbers yet. Emphasis on calibrated, efficiency-first retail expansion ("not chasing numbers").
non-obvious points:
- FY26 revenue guidance UPGRADE (10–12% → 12–15%) called "an exception" given their usual annual-only stance — notable positive signal.
- Exports are **indirect** (fabric → converters → brands); FTA benefit is second-order, not direct shipment to EU brands.
- Larger-format stores (6,000–8,000 sq ft) chosen after explicit A/B experiment vs small format.
- Indigo yarn business quietly grown to ~5–6% within Yarn & Others.
- Q3 store openings deliberately throttled to protect festive operations (lean team) — Q2 front-loaded the openings.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A 48-year-old Mumbai-headquartered textile and apparel company, among India's most renowned marketers of premium fabrics and readymade menswear, now expanding into fast-fashion and ethnic-wear retail through 'Siyaram 2.0'.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Siyaram Silk Mills manufactures and markets fabrics (poly-viscose, cotton, wool, linen, bamboo and stretch blends), readymade menswear (shirts, trousers, blazers and suits) and dyed/indigo yarn, sold under established brands including Siyaram's, J. Hampstead, Cadini, Oxemberg and Mistair. It has recently launched two new retail formats, ZECODE (fast fashion) and DEVO (ethnic wear), rolled out through company-owned stores in cluster-based markets.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Consumer demand was uneven through FY26 — early-year softness from seasonal disruption and cautious discretionary spending, restored momentum in festive/wedding periods, and gradual improvement toward year-end supported by tax reform measures and higher spending around key consumption periods
- India's consumption story is seen as a meaningful long-term opportunity, supported by rising aspirations, improving incomes, a growing preference for branded products and expanding retail infrastructure
- Industry continues to navigate elevated input and logistics costs, inflationary pressures and an evolving geopolitical environment as cost/margin headwinds
- Domestic demand remains sensitive to discretionary spending patterns and inflation, with a shift toward value pricing pressuring margins in mass-market apparel

- Global brands' 'China+1' sourcing shift is strengthening India's position as a reliable manufacturing hub, supporting export opportunity

scorecard (q3 fy26):
| Metric | Q3 FY26 | Q3 FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | ₹639 cr | ₹586 cr | +8.9% | Festive demand picked up early then footfall moderated; "occasion-driven" |
| 9M FY26 income | ₹1,782 cr | ₹1,546 cr | +15.3% | Strong 9M; Diwali fell early in quarter → much of festive sales landed in Q2 |
| EBITDA | ₹84 cr | ₹83 cr | +1.5% | Held absolute EBITDA despite cost pressure |
| EBITDA margin | 13.2% | 14.1% | −90 bps | Down on one-offs + retail losses |
| 9M EBITDA / margin | ₹262 cr | — | — | Margin 14.7% |
| PAT | ₹42 cr | ₹46 cr | −8.7% | PAT DOWN YoY; margin 6.6% |
| 9M PAT / margin | ₹134 cr | — | — | Margin 7.5% |
| Revenue mix | Fabric 78% · Garment 15% · Yarn & Others 7% | — | — | Fabric down from north-of-80% historically |

**Revenue by segment (Q3 mix):** Fabric 78%, Garment 15%, Yarn & Others 7% (Indigo ~5–6% within Yarn & Others). Exports ~9–10% of revenue, largely fabric.

**Seasonality CALL-OUT:** Highly seasonal — mgmt repeatedly discouraged QoQ reads. Diwali timing (early in Q3) shifted festive sales into Q2, depressing Q3 textile growth (~3% YoY) vs strong 9M. **Q4 is "the best quarter of the year"** (wedding season); inventory being built up for it (drove higher working capital & processing/labour charges).

**One-offs (explicit, ~₹10–12 cr combined drag):** (1) onetime employee expense from the **new labour code**; (2) higher **advertising & sales promotion**; (3) **new-retail (ZECODE/DEVO) start-up losses** (in line with guided 100–150 bps EBITDA drag).
guidance (critical):
- **FY26 revenue growth RAISED to 12–15%** (from prior 10–12%) — overall company. Described as "an exception" to their usual annual-only guidance.
- **FY26 EBITDA margin ~14%** (approx, ex-retail), to be reduced by **100–150 bps** from retail (ZECODE/DEVO) losses.
- **Retail (ZECODE+DEVO) revenue ₹70–80 cr for FY26** — ₹55 cr done in 9M; on track / in line.
- **Store rollout: ~35 ZECODE+DEVO stores in FY26.** ~22 opened YTD; Q3 added only 2 ZECODE + 5 DEVO (intentionally slow to focus ops on festive). Cumulative: ZECODE 25, DEVO 17. Balance to be opened by March (possible spillover).
- Fabric volume growth **~9% (9M FY26)**; suiting vs shirting differ — mgmt prefers value over volume reads.
- **FY27 guidance (revenue, margin, store plans, new geographies) deferred to next quarter.**
demand:
- Festive demand picked up at start of quarter, then customers turned cautious, footfall moderate; demand **occasion/festive-driven**, spikes at key events, not a sustained trend.
- Discretionary spend high in festive season across BOTH premium and mass/value fabrics — "more festive driven than price-point driven"; value audience much larger → larger numbers.
- New retail growing faster than traditional business; "very encouraging" wedding-season traction for ZECODE/DEVO, better footfall and repeat customers.
segment detail:
- **Fabric (78%):** Suiting (poly-viscose to woollen blends) + shirting (polycotton, cotton, linen blends); few branded players, **no meaningful pricing pressure**; gross-margin moves driven by product mix. ~9% 9M volume growth. Has been declining as % (from >80% historically) as other segments scale.
- **Garment / branded apparel (15%):** Siyaram's, J.Hampstead, Oxemberg branded business.
- **Yarn & Others (7%):** Includes an **Indigo business growing to ~5–6%**.
- **New retail — ZECODE & DEVO:** First full year of operation; nascent, more stores opening than running; ₹55 cr in 9M; offline-only for now (no e-commerce yet); large-format (6,000–8,000 sq ft) preferred over small (4,000–6,000) after experimentation; regional clusters (ZECODE in one region, DEVO in another); sourcing/gross-margin still a start-up challenge.
growth / optionality:
- **Branded value-retail scale-up (ZECODE/DEVO)** — calibrated, self-owned model; expects to become a "meaningful part" of turnover over years; e-commerce/omnichannel "at the back of our minds" for later.
- **Exports (~9–10%, largely fabric to converters):** Beneficiary of India-as-manufacturing-hub narrative, govt manufacturing push, and **new FTAs (incl. European FTA)** — indirect benefit (fabric supplied to garment converters who serve brands).
- **Forward integration:** Exploring expansion of **garment infrastructure to supply formal trousers** (not just suiting fabric) → could become a direct supplier; "some time away".
- **CADINI (Italian brand/subsidiary):** exposes company to European fashion/trends, feeds design USP.
margins & cost:
- EBITDA margin 13.2% (−90 bps YoY) on: new labour-code employee one-off, higher ad/sales promotion, retail start-up losses (~₹10–12 cr combined ex-retail-loss items).
- **Marketing/ad spend guided at 4–5% of revenue** (includes both legacy and new brands; new brands more regional/digital) — treated as brand-building investment.
- Gross margin up ~3% YoY on product mix (mgmt expects balanced/stable full-year).
- Processing & labour charges rose ~14%→15% of net sales due to inventory build for Q4.
- Steady-state retail margin not yet disclosed (sourcing/gross-margin challenges; will share "in a few quarters").
capex:
- **Legacy: asset-light, maintenance capex ~₹50–70 cr/year** (sufficient internal cash flow).
- **Retail: ~₹35–40 cr for FY26** (calibrated).
capital allocation:
- **Second interim dividend of ₹3/share** (face value ₹2) declared.
- Disciplined/"prudent" capital allocation; legacy cash funds retail rollout; "well within comfort limit" on debt.
- Finance cost up YoY due to extra working capital for inventory build; expected to improve by Q4 end.
- Open to partnerships/acquisitions but nothing currently planned; focus on existing retail brands.
risks:
- **Demand:** weak/occasion-driven discretionary spend; cautious consumer, moderate footfall.
- **Seasonality / timing:** Diwali timing skew distorts quarterly reads; heavy Q4 dependence.
- **Retail execution:** nascent ZECODE/DEVO, sourcing & gross-margin challenges, lean team, near-term EBITDA drag (100–150 bps).
- **Cost:** new labour-code one-off; elevated ad spend; higher working capital → finance cost.
- **Competition:** large unorganized apparel market (sees as headroom, not direct threat); fabric segment has few branded peers / no pricing pressure cited.
- Note: textile growth (~3% Q3) lagged peer Raymond (~11%) — attributed to Diwali timing.
management tone: Measured, disciplined, defensive on QoQ ("not advisable to look quarterly — seasonal business"), confident on raised FY26 guidance. Cautious/transparent on retail being early-stage; declines to give store-level economics or FY27 numbers yet. Emphasis on calibrated, efficiency-first retail expansion ("not chasing numbers").
non-obvious points:
- FY26 revenue guidance UPGRADE (10–12% → 12–15%) called "an exception" given their usual annual-only stance — notable positive signal.
- Exports are **indirect** (fabric → converters → brands); FTA benefit is second-order, not direct shipment to EU brands.
- Larger-format stores (6,000–8,000 sq ft) chosen after explicit A/B experiment vs small format.
- Indigo yarn business quietly grown to ~5–6% within Yarn & Others.
- Q3 store openings deliberately throttled to protect festive operations (lean team) — Q2 front-loaded the openings.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅/⭐ (none explicitly flagged as actionable third-party beneficiary plays)
- Self-relevant tailwind: India manufacturing-hub + FTA push → potential beneficiary as fabric/garment exporter; possible future direct formal-trouser supplier.

---
qoq log: - **Q3 FY26 (this call):** Total income ₹639 cr (+8.9% YoY); EBITDA ₹84 cr (+1.5%), margin 13.2% (−90 bps); PAT ₹42 cr (−8.7%), margin 6.6%. Mix Fabric 78% / Garment 15% / Yarn&Others 7%. FY26 rev guidance RAISED 10–12% → 12–15%; EBITDA ~14% ex-retail, −100/150 bps retail drag. Retail ₹55 cr/9M vs ₹70–80 cr FY26 target; stores ZECODE 25 / DEVO 17 (added 2+5 in Q3); ~35-store FY26 plan. 2nd interim dividend ₹3/sh. One-offs: new labour-code employee cost + higher ad spend (~₹10–12 cr) + retail start-up losses. FY27 guidance deferred to next quarter.

themes.title: Branded innerwear & domestic apparel
themes.need: Branded innerwear and domestic apparel are driven by rural recovery, GST 2.0 and distribution reach - a domestic-consumption thesis, not the China+1/FTA export tailwind powering exporters and synthetics.
themes.driver: Rural recovery + GST 2.0 demand pull and distribution-led volume growth.

hero.oneLiner: A 48-year-old Mumbai-headquartered textile and apparel company, among India's most renowned marketers of premium fabrics and readymade menswear, now expanding into fast-fashion and ethnic-wear retail through 'Siyaram 2.0'.
